run_purpose.description: A closed vocabulary, not free text: each value is tied to a documented decision rule (CLAUDE.md section 11-12), so 'a run_purpose exists' is a structural fact the schema can enforce, not a trust-the-caller string.

run_outcome.description: Whether this specific run actually completed and produced a usable comparison signal. POLICY (see domain/runtime/evaluation-usage-ledger.mjs): a DISTINCT run_id consumes the DEV_CHECK/HOLDOUT run budget regardless of SUCCESS or FAILURE — the current minimal implementation treats every recorded official execution attempt as data exposure, since there is no separate exposure_started/attempt state to distinguish 'crashed before touching data' from 'crashed after'. FAILURE is recorded for audit completeness, not to grant a free retry against the same budget.

assigned_split_at_use.description: Audit copy of the assignment's evaluation-split-lifecycle.schema.json assigned_split at the moment this event was appended — lets a later auditor confirm executed_split was actually consistent with the assignment's pinned split (or, for a SANDBOX execution, see what it was ultimately pinned to) without needing to replay lifecycle history.

holdout_lifecycle_status_at_use.description: Audit copy of holdout_lifecycle_status at the moment this event was appended. Present on every event (not just HOLDOUT-executed ones) for a uniform, unconditional schema shape; for a non-HOLDOUT-assigned item this is simply whatever the (unused) default lifecycle state was.

previous_log_hash.description: The event_hash of the immediately preceding event in this ledger, or null only for the very first (genesis) event. Forms a simple linear hash chain — see domain/runtime/evaluation-usage-ledger.mjs's KNOWN LIMITATION note on what this chain can and cannot detect.

event_hash.description: SHA-256 of this event's own canonical JSON content (every other field, including previous_log_hash) with event_hash itself excluded from what's hashed.
